title: Container With Most Water
description: You are given an integer array height of length n. There are n vertical lines drawn such that the two endpoints of line i are (i, 0) and (i, height[i]). Find two lines that, together with the x-axis, form a container that holds the most water. Return the maximum amount of water it can store.

examples.explanation: Lines at index 1 (height 8) and index 8 (height 7): min(8,7) * (8-1) = 7*7 = 49.

hints: Start with the widest container (two outer pointers). Moving the taller line inward can only shrink the width without helping the height — always move the shorter line inward instead.

testCases.description: Best answer uses the two outermost lines

optimalSolution.approach: Two pointers starting at both ends. At each step compute the area, then move whichever pointer points at the shorter line inward — that's the only move that could possibly increase the area.

followUpQuestions: Why is it always safe to move the shorter line's pointer, never the taller one?
Could this container ever be improved by moving both pointers inward at once?
How is this different from Trapping Rain Water, which looks superficially similar?
interviewerNotes: The greedy justification ("why move the shorter pointer") is the real test — a candidate who gets the right code by pattern-matching 'two pointer' without being able to justify the greedy step hasn't fully understood it.
